text:
[LSER.19.8] **A cold read yields `null`, at the grain of this partition.** An
aggregation read is **cold** when its backing holds no sample to aggregate for
that identity — before the first absorption, or once every absorbed sample has
left the window. `active_fraction` and `integral` are the exception to the
second: they aggregate a step function, in which each asserted value holds
until the next ([LSIG.1.3.1], [LSIG.3.2]), so the last absorbed value reaches
into every later window and their read is cold only before the first
absorption. The engine **must** answer a cold read with the value below,
not with an error and not with a placeholder. Reading a cold series is a normal
thing for a rule to do on the first pumps after start or restart.

**These keep a concrete return type**, because zero is the honest answer rather
than a stand-in for one:

| Aggregation | Cold value |
|---|---|
| `count`, `count_distinct`, `count_of` | `0` |
| `contains` | `false` |
| `sum` | `0` |
| `active_fraction`, `onset_rate`, `integral` | `0.0` |

Nothing has been observed, so the count **is** zero and the value **has not**
been seen. `[LSIG.8.1]` is retained unchanged by this clause, not overridden.

**Every other aggregation is genuinely undefined when cold and its declared
return type is therefore `T?` ([LSER.16]),** yielding `null` while cold. This
includes `bool_and` / `bool_or`: a universal over an empty series is not `true`
and an existential over one is not `false` — those are the *vacuous* answers,
and returning them would let a rule fire on a series that has told it nothing.
The descriptive, dispersion, quantile and temporal families are undefined for
the same reason — there is no mean of nothing.

**A cold read needs no guard in a `where` predicate.** A `null` propagates
through comparison and boolean operators and a `where` fires only on `true`
([LNUL.4.3]), so a rule reading a cold `T?` aggregation does not fire until the
backing holds a sample. At a concrete-value position the `T?` is rescued with
`??` or written to a `T?` slot ([LNUL.5.1]).

Whether a
read has a value is the read's own answer. An aggregation that needs more than
one sample says so in its own definition: `stdev`, `variance` and `direction`
are also `null` while one sample is held, and `rate` while no time separates
the first and last ([LSER.17.2]). This holds on every backing, a `sample n`
reservoir included: before its bag is full the bag holds every absorbed
sample ([LSMP.2.1]), and its aggregations are read over those.
